seoTitle: Collapse and Expand Rows in Smartsheet Easily
metaDescription: Manage multi-level task structures in Smartsheet by collapsing and expanding rows, using bulk commands, and understanding how it affects rollups.
intro: Once your sheet has dozens of subtasks under each phase, scrolling gets exhausting. Smartsheet's collapse and expand controls let you hide granular detail and focus on high-level milestones. This guide covers setting up hierarchies, using the toggles, and understanding how collapsed rows interact with your data rollups.

steps.heading: Build a parent-child hierarchy
steps.body: Indent rows directly under master milestones to establish a proper task hierarchy.

steps.heading: Use the expand/collapse toggles
steps.body: Locate the small +/- or arrow toggles in the primary task column to hide granular subtasks instantly.

steps.heading: Collapse or expand everything at once
steps.body: Use the right-click row menu or toolbar to run bulk Collapse All or Expand All operations.

steps.heading: Check other views
steps.body: Confirm your row groupings stay intact when switching between Grid View, Card View, and Gantt Chart layouts.

steps.heading: Understand rollup behavior
steps.body: Know that collapsing rows doesn't affect summary formulas or child-row data rollups, which continue calculating in the background.

faq.question: Does collapsing rows hide data from formulas too?
faq.answer: No, collapsed rows still contribute to summary formulas and child-row data rollups; collapsing only affects the visual display.

faq.question: Can I collapse all rows on my sheet at once?
faq.answer: Yes, the right-click row menu and toolbar both offer Collapse All and Expand All commands for bulk management.

faq.question: Will collapsed rows stay collapsed in Gantt view?
faq.answer: Indented row groupings generally carry over across Grid, Card, and Gantt views, though it's worth double-checking after switching.

faq.question: How do I quickly find hidden collapsed sections?
faq.answer: Reviewing the expander icons in the primary task column helps you identify which sections are currently collapsed.
